events.title: Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season
events.summary:
Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding

Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

As a result of the strong El Niño, it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered.

events.title: France Protests, Israel's 'politically charged' remembrance, Ethopia, Ukraine
events.summary: It’s been a week of vigils, protests and political upheaval – from Israel, where three years after the Hamas-led attacks, former hostages and mourners called for accountability over the failures of October 7th, as questions grow over the stalled path to peace in Gaza; to France, where mass demonstrations over chronic underfunding and poor conditions have drawn students, unions and hundreds of thousands of protesters into the streets, just months ahead of a presidential election. And in the UK, questions remain over a suspected Iranian plot targeting US aircraft at RAF Fairford, after American B-1 bombers were hastily withdrawn amid warnings of a serious and immediate threat.

events.title: Navi Pillay awarded Peace Prize: 'Lifetime spent fighting for what's right & to uphold human rights'
events.summary: Haxie Meyers-Belkin is pleased to welcome Rosa Freedman, Professor of Law Conflict and Global Development at the University of Reading. Navi Pillay's career represents a remarkable contribution to international law and human rights, from her pioneering role in post-apartheid South Africa to her work at the United Nations. Yet her legacy also raises difficult questions about political impartiality, particularly in relation to Israel and Gaza. She believes we need to distinguish between the significance of her lifelong achievements and the controversy surrounding the decision to award her the Nobel Peace Prize at this particular moment. More broadly, this debate invites us to examine whether the prize is recognising individual merit or increasingly serving as a vehicle for political messaging. At a time when international law and multilateral institutions face mounting pressure, and serious threats, Freedman asserts that the challenge is to scrutinise their shortcomings without undermining the principles they exist to uphold.

events.title: 🔴 FlyDubai co-pilot planned suicide attack on Tel Aviv airport, inspired by 9/11, UAE prosecutor says

events.title: Unweaving Jeffrey Epstein’s web: What the files have revealed
events.summary: On January 30, 2026, the US Justice Department released 3 million documents. Photos, videos, emails, text messages, court records... All connected to one man: Jeffrey Epstein. Since then, media outlets around the world have brought to light the vast amount of people that appear in the Epstein files. Eight months on, what what do these revelations tell us about Jeffrey Epstein’s network? How did it operate? FRANCE 24 journalist Ava Luquet spent months digging through the files. In this video, she takes a closer look at what they reveal about the predator’s network and its inner workings.

events.title: Le Pen's top ally Bardella faces fresh claims he sought to cover up past anti-Semitic comments

events.title: EU's Covid recovery fund was 'absolutely a success': European Court of Auditors' Pierre Moscovici
events.summary: 2020 was an annus horribilis. Covid stalked the land. Lockdowns, curfews and social distancing were the order of the day. But there was a silver lining: European countries showed themselves to be capable of great solidarity, jointly procuring vaccines and then agreeing on a mammoth post-Covid recovery fund, the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF). That fund has disbursed €450 billion in grants and loans to EU member states since 2021. As the RRF enters its crucial final phase, we take stock of the situation with Pierre Moscovici, the French member of the European Court of Auditors (ECA).

events.title: 2026 Nobel Peace Prize: Who is Navanethem “Navi” Pillay?
events.summary: The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to South African Navanethem “Navi” Pillay on Friday, October 9, 2026. events.title: 2027 spring-summer ready-to-wear collections: Audacity, movement and sensuality
events.summary: We bring you all the latest from Paris Fashion Week. For Weinsanto, audacity is about finding a lightness, as embodied by the LGBTQ+ community. At Issey Miyake, it's about sensuality rooted in the Japanese concept of Ma, the space that bridges the gap between fabric and skin. events.title: Israel a rare dissenting voice as praise pours in for Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay

events.title: International Criminal Court faces 'test of resilience' as US imposes sweeping sanctions

The PISA test is an international assessment led by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), which measures how well 15‑year‑olds in over 80 countries apply reading, mathematics and science skills to real‑world problems. In the latest rankings, France's results were the worst it has ever had, and Germany's school pupils got their worst PISA report card too.

events.title: Lawsuits blame Fox News for deaths of journalists in Ukraine

Reporter Benjamin Hall was seriously injured and two other journalists were killed. The journalists' families are suing Fox, saying the network put the story ahead of its people. events.title: 'Absolute torture': Female US inmate in critical condition after botched execution
events.summary: A condemned female murderer who survived two lethal injections during a botched execution by the US state of Tennessee was in critical condition and receiving "life-saving care," according to her attorneys. In an extraordinary chain of events, Christa Pike, 50, was whisked from a prison execution chamber to a hospital, still alive despite two deadly doses of pentobarbital. What happened to Pike is "absolute torture," said Sandrine Ageorges-Skinner, Spokesperson for Together Against the Death Penalty (ECPM), speaking to FRANCE 24's Alison Sargent.

events.title: Sierra Leone: From 'blood diamonds' to stones of hope?

Accused of complicity in the conflict, the diamond industry has since sought to clean up its image, emphasising an ethical shift. But a quarter of a century on, have the former "blood diamonds" truly become synonymous with development? FRANCE 24's Sarah Sakho and Simon Martin report.

events.title: Russia says all clear after contact tracing in reported plague case

events.title: No peace without international law: The message behind Navi Pillay’s Nobel

events.title: U.S. ends ISIS-fighting mission in Iraq as regional security fears mount
events.summary: Kurdish officials are worried the Biden-era decision was being carried out after Iranian missiles pummeled them this year.

events.title: Iran ‘fully prepared’ for war to resume but diplomacy not over yet, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says
events.summary: Despite Trump’s comments rejecting a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Araghchi said Iran hadn’t yet officially responded to the proposal.

events.title: Warrants used to search former Prince Andrew's homes were unlawful, court says
events.summary: Police who searched the properties of the former Prince Andrew and seized his property in the investigation into his links to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein have agreed the search warrants were unlawful, a London judge said. NBC News' India McTaggart reports.

events.title: Clashes erupt between French police and protesters demanding better schools
events.summary: Police charged demonstrators with clubs and fired tear gas as protesters resisted a crackdown, vowing to keep fighting for what they say are France’s broken schools. NBC News’ Richard Engel reports.

events.title: WHO seeks answers and clarity over plague lab death in Russia
events.summary: The World Health Organization is pushing for more answers and clarity in the plague death that happened in a lab in Russia. NBC News' Dr. Akshay Syal has more on what we know about the illness and what WHO is seeking from Russia.

events.title: Emotional ceremonies mark three years since Hamas terror attacks
events.summary: Emotional ceremonies across the world marked three years since the Hamas terror attacks on Israel. NBC News’ Keir Simmons reports.

events.title: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to discuss ‘new’ peace plan with Ukrainian delegation, sources say
events.summary: Ukrainian negotiators heading to the United States for a new round of talks to end the war with Russia will discuss a comprehensive new plan to help break the ongoing impasse in the conflict, a senior administration official told NBC News.

events.title: What to know about pneumonic plague after woman in Russia dies from mysterious illness
events.summary: The death of a 28-year-old woman who worked in an anti-plague laboratory in Russia is raising concerns about what caused her illness.

events.title: At least 30 people killed as Russia bombs two buses in Ukraine
events.summary: Images from the scene in eastern Ukraine showed bodies and body parts strewed across a road and the burned shells of the buses.

events.title: Russia says no plague found in contacts of Siberian lab worker who died
events.summary: News that a female staffer had died from a “pneumonia of undetermined” origin last week has spread fears worldwide.

events.title: U.S. resident charged with helping Canadian school shooter in rampage that killed 8
events.summary: Jesse Van Rootselaar, 18, killed her mother and stepbrother and then five students and a teacher at a secondary school in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, in February.

events.title: Flydubai pilot planned a 9/11-style attack on Tel Aviv airport, source says
events.summary: The suspect was being questioned by investigators in the United Arab Emirates.

events.title: Iranian drone threat prompted U.S. to remove bombers from British base, officials say
events.summary: The bombers at RAF Fairford “have been re-deployed to their home stations in the United States,” a Pentagon official told NBC News.

events.title: BA flight to Chicago drops 28,000 feet, returns to London
events.summary: About 30 minutes into its journey, the aircraft dropped from 36,000 feet to 9,000 feet in around seven minutes, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware.

events.title: 200 people enter medical observation after worker at Russian anti-plague lab dies
events.summary: The female staffer at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East died from a “pneumonia of undetermined” origin last week, according to a regional governor.

events.title: Russia pounds Kyiv during German chancellor’s visit in a new escalation
events.summary: Germany’s foreign intel chief warns it could become embroiled in a conflict with Russia as Moscow steps up its “shadow war” against European democracies.

events.title: Early indications suggest Flydubai co-pilot acted alone in attack, officials say
events.summary: Officials cautioned that the investigation remains in its early stages and that possible links to an organization or foreign government haven’t been definitively ruled out.

events.title: U.S. Marine arrested on suspicion of killing Japanese woman in Okinawa
events.summary: Japan’s Defense Ministry said it was “deeply outraged by the extremely brutal and heinous crime committed by a U.S. Marine.”

events.title: Flydubai pilot attacked captain with cockpit’s crash ax in attempted terrorist act, UAE official says
events.summary: TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.

events.title: Two Iranian nationals charged over alleged terrorism plot targeting Jewish community in England
events.summary: British police said Friday that they had charged two Iranian nationals accused of plotting a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

events.title: Screaming, panicking, blood: Passengers detail horrifying Israel-bound flight
events.summary: It was too early to say why a pilot stabbed another on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

events.title: What we know about the cockpit stabbing on Israel-bound flight
events.summary: What we know about the potential midair disaster aboard the Flydubai flight when a pilot attacked his colleague causing the plane to plunge thousands of feet.
